questions.why: The informational text on the right mentions 'Clinical Summaries' as an available option, but there is no corresponding section in the main layout to actually access them.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness that a specific type of medical record might be missing or inaccessible despite being advertised by the portal.

questions.question: Do the on-screen instructions match the available interface elements?
questions.why: The instructions direct you to choose a provider by typing their name in a search box, but no search box is present on the screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to complete the e-Visit if the agent gets stuck looking for a non-existent search box to select a provider.

questions.question: Does the scheduled appointment date align with the current system clock?
questions.why: The appointment details show a visit scheduled for Wednesday, April 08, 2020, but the system clock indicates it is Tuesday, raising doubts about the validity of the check-in.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the agent is checking in for a genuinely upcoming appointment rather than interacting with outdated or simulated data.

questions.question: Do you notice that the current medication widget says there are 8 medications, but only lists 3?
questions.why: The widget header claims 8 medications are on file, but only three specific drugs are visible on the screen, meaning important medical information might be hidden or missing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might just record the three visible medications and fail to alert you that five other prescriptions are missing from the view.

questions.question: Do the appointments shown on the dashboard match what is listed on the upcoming appointments page?
questions.why: The dashboard widget displayed a single appointment for 05/04/2020, while the upcoming appointments page listed three different dates.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might only look at the dashboard summary and fail to notify you about all of your actual upcoming visits.

questions.question: Are the timestamps on the completion banner and the system clock consistent?
questions.why: The registration banner states the form was completed at 10:00 AM, but the system clock reads 9:47 AM, revealing an impossible timeline.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to catch and correct system errors or time zone mismatches in their official medical records.

questions.question: Are you checking in the same patient you started with?
questions.why: The eCheck-In screen listed the patient name as 'Zola, Eighteen', but the waiting room screen displayed 'Eighteen Ztdv'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty that the agent is managing the correct patient's appointment and medical records.

questions.question: Does the review screen accurately reflect the choices you made on the previous screen?
questions.why: The review screen lists 'None of these' for symptoms, even though this selection was not shown on the previous screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses confidence that their health screening answers are being accurately recorded and submitted.

questions.question: Are you okay with the final confirmation stating you might still need to sign documents upon arrival, despite having just signed them?
questions.why: The portal marked your documents as 'Signed' during the flow, but the final confirmation screen warns you might still need to sign documents upon arrival.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might ignore this contradictory warning, leaving you unprepared for unexpected paperwork when you arrive at the clinic.

questions.question: What follow-up instructions should you review?
questions.why: The screen explains how prescriptions are handled, how insurance is billed, and exactly where to find your after-visit summary.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss the direct understanding of the next steps for your care, billing, and medical records.

questions.question: Do you want to start the process of inviting someone to access your health information?
questions.why: The screen warns that sharing your record allows another person to see, update, or delete your potentially sensitive health information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose direct control over deciding who gets access to your highly sensitive medical records and what permissions they receive.

questions.question: What email address and passcode should I use for this invitation?
questions.why: The screen requires a recipient email address and a custom passcode of at least four characters to secure the invitation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose the recipient and securely communicate the custom passcode to them through a separate channel.

questions.question: What level of access should you grant to this person?
questions.why: The portal requires you to choose between read-only or read-and-modify access, which dictates whether the recipient can alter your medical records or just view them.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent decides how much control another person has over your sensitive health information.

questions.question: Which types of medical information do you want to share?
questions.why: The screen requires you to choose between sharing all types of information or manually selecting specific types to share.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means an agent might overshare sensitive health details that you would have preferred to keep private.

questions.question: Do you want to set an expiration date for sharing your health information?
questions.why: The screen required choosing between entering a specific access expiration date or selecting a 'No expiration date' radio button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to control exactly how long the recipient will have access to their sensitive medical records.

questions.question: Are you ready to send this invitation with the configured settings?
questions.why: The screen presents 'Send Invitation' and 'Cancel' buttons, requiring a final confirmation before the system processes the request and returns to the dashboard.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the recipient and access settings before granting someone access to your health information.

questions.question: Whose access settings do you want to modify?
questions.why: The screen lists multiple individuals with access to the health record, and you must select the specific person whose permissions need updating.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means an agent might alter the wrong person's access to your sensitive medical information.

questions.question: What access level should you grant, and should you restrict the information types or set an expiration date?
questions.why: The screen provides options to grant 'Read only' or 'Read and modify' access, along with settings for specific information types and expiration dates, which dictate how much control another person has over your medical record.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally decide the exact boundaries and duration of access someone else has to your sensitive health information.

questions.question: How do you save the new access settings?
questions.why: The modal displays options to change, cancel, or remove access, requiring you to select the correct button to apply the new permissions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally verify and confirm the exact level of medical record access being granted.

questions.question: Which option should I select from your profile menu?
questions.why: The profile menu contains several distinct actions, such as managing the account, sharing records, viewing record history, or signing out.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over which account management or sharing feature is accessed, or if they are signed out prematurely.

questions.question: Which account management option do you want to select from the dropdown menu?
questions.why: The dropdown menu presents several choices, including 'Record History' which tracks deleted items and account changes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide which specific account management feature to access.

questions.question: Where do you click to verify or update your contact phone number?
questions.why: The dropdown menu shows a 'Patient Information' option where personal details like your telephone number are stored.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent skips clicking this option, you lose the ability to actually verify or update your contact details on screen.

questions.question: Where do you find the option to share your health record?
questions.why: The option to share your record is tucked away in the dropdown menu under your profile initials, alongside other account management settings.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the knowledge of where your record sharing and profile management settings are located within the portal for future use.

questions.question: Whose health record do you want to view?
questions.why: The profile menu displays multiple linked accounts, so you must specify which person's health information to access.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might access or act upon the wrong family member's medical record.

questions.question: Is the dependent's profile missing or grayed out due to automatically expired proxy access?
questions.why: Proxy access for minors often automatically expires or severely restricts data visibility on their 12th or 18th birthday due to state privacy laws, requiring new legal authorization.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might silently fail to find the child's record or access the wrong profile, leaving the user unaware that their legal access rights have lapsed.

questions.question: Which credentials should you provide to link the account?
questions.why: The screen requires a specific username and password to authorize linking your health records.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires sharing sensitive login credentials for a secondary health account with the agent.

questions.question: Where do you initiate the process to link another account?
questions.why: The dashboard displays an 'Account' section with a 'View Linked Accounts' dropdown that must be expanded to manage family or dependent records.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose immediate visibility into which family members' accounts are currently connected to your profile.

questions.question: Do you agree to the proxy access terms to view the dependent's records?
questions.why: The portal requires you to accept the proxy access terms and conditions before it will share the dependent's medical information with you.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to read and personally consent to the specific legal terms regarding access to your dependent's medical records.

questions.question: Do you want to bookmark the portal for easy access later?
questions.why: The screen shows a bookmark popup offering to save the portal's address to your bookmarks bar.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to choose a recognizable name or specific folder for the saved bookmark.

questions.question: How do you securely log out of the patient portal?
questions.why: The top navigation menu provides a 'Logout' tab to safely end your session and protect your health information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you cannot personally confirm that your sensitive medical account was securely closed.

questions.question: How should you clear the session?
questions.why: The 'Thank You' screen indicates the task is complete, requiring the app to be fully closed to protect patient privacy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the certainty of personally verifying that your private health session was completely terminated.
